reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Bypass obstruction, ventilate long, clear secretions
First tube change after tract matures (about day 5 to 7)
Sentinel bleed means vessel erosion until disproven
Decannulate on capping plus swallow plus secretions
reference.pathophysiology: Prolonged translaryngeal tubes ulcerate posterior glottis and subglottis while tracheostomy redirects airflow below injured segments; cuff overpressure ischaemiates tracheal mucosa circumferentially, healing by granulation then stenosis, and low anterior erosion reaches innominate artery where it crosses.
additionalDifferentials: Tracheostomy versus prolonged intubation by duration and secretion burden
Cricothyrotomy versus tracheostomy by urgency and stenosis risk
Foreign body versus croup or asthma by sudden onset and laterality
additionalInvestigations: Bedside airway assessment, cuff pressure manometry
Chest films inspiratory and expiratory for air trapping
